Getting Started with scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulations

Kabilan Sakthivel, Dr. Dwijesh Chandra Mishra, Dr. Shashi Bhushan Lal, Dr. Ulavappa Angadi, Dr. Sudhir Srivastava, Dr. Neeraj Budhlakoti, Dr. Krishna Kumar Chaturvedi, Dr. Ranjeet Ranjan Kumar, Dr. Navin Chandra Gupta, Dr. Sharanbasappa

2026-11-13

Source: vignettes/scSimEval-workflow.Rmd
scSimEval-workflow.Rmd

1. Introduction

Computer simulations of single-cell technologies—specifically single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), single-cell ATAC sequencing (scATAC-seq), and scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq multiomics—are essential in bioinformatics for developing pipelines, optimizing analysis workflows, and evaluating statistical methods. A fundamental question for any benchmark is: how realistically does the simulated data replicate genuine biological experiments?

scSimEval provides a standardized, reference-based benchmarking framework computing 56 curated evaluation measures across 8 foundational categories:

  1. Experimental reference data (ref_rna, ref_atac)
  2. Simulated synthetic data (sim_rna, sim_atac)
  3. Cell type annotations (cell_types, optional)
  4. Batch or donor identifiers (batch_info, optional)
  5. Computer resources (Core-seconds and memory footprint per core in MiB)
  6. Developmental trajectories (automatically inferred directly from count matrices)

Figure 1: Unified benchmarking architecture of scSimEval. The end-to-end framework ingests reference and simulated single-cell and multiomics count matrices with experimental metadata, evaluates 56 curated evaluation measures across eight biological and computational dimensions, standardizes scores via direction-aware normalization, and generates publication-grade comparative visualizations and leaderboards.

Supported Multiomics Modalities: scSimEval natively supports two multiomics experimental designs:4 Paired (co-assays where RNA and ATAC are measured from identical cells, e.g. 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq) with full cross-modal coupling evaluation; and Unpaired (independent scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq from separate cells of the same tissue) with unimodal evaluation plus population-level cross-modal concordance metrics. See the dedicated Multiomics vignette for detailed multiomics workflows.

2. Input Data Formats and Metric Measurement Capacity

2.1 Input Data Formats & Metadata Requirements

scSimEval accepts standard single-cell count matrices and optional metadata:

  1. Count Matrices (ref, sim):

    • Dimensions: Features (Genes or ATAC Peaks) in rows ×\times Cells in columns.
    • Data Types: R sparse matrices (dgCMatrix), standard numeric matrices, data.frame, SingleCellExperiment, or Seurat.

  2. Cell-Type Annotations (cell_types, optional):

    • Used for Category III clustering fidelity (ARI, NMI, Silhouette width) and Category V biological signal preservation.

    • Character vector or factor matching cell columns:

      data(example_cell_types, package = "scSimEval")
head(example_cell_types)
# Cell_01 Cell_02 Cell_03 Cell_04 Cell_05 
#   TypeA   TypeA   TypeA   TypeA   TypeA

  3. Batch Annotations (batch_info, optional):

    • Used for Category IV batch effect and confounder mixing metrics (CMS, Inverse Simpson’s Index, PCR R2R^2, Batch Silhouette, Seurat mixing, cross-batch F1).

    • Character vector or factor matching cell columns:

      data(example_batch_info, package = "scSimEval")
head(example_batch_info)
# Cell_01 Cell_02 Cell_03 Cell_04 Cell_05 
#  Batch1  Batch2  Batch1  Batch2  Batch1

  4. Exporting Annotations from Seurat or SingleCellExperiment:

    # From Seurat:
cell_types <- as.character(Idents(seurat_obj))
batch_info <- as.character(seurat_obj$batch)

# From SingleCellExperiment:
cell_types <- as.character(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)$cell_type)
batch_info <- as.character(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)$batch)

2.2 Metric Measurement Capacity by Data & Metadata Mode

scSimEval automatically scales its evaluation depth based on the input matrices and metadata provided. The exact metric counts measured by the updated package across the built-in reference datasets (example_scrna, example_scatac, example_rice_bud, and example_soybean_root) are summarized below:

Experiment Mode Uploaded Inputs Metrics Measured Active Evaluation Categories & Scope
Single-Cell (scRNA / scATAC) Count Matrix alone (no metadata) 19 Metrics (scRNA) / 14 (scATAC) Cat I (Distributional Properties), Cat II (Sparsity & Zeroes), Cat III (Cellular Manifolds), Cat VII (dynverse Trajectory: 5 metrics, scRNA-seq only), and Cat VIII (Scalability).
Single-Cell (scRNA / scATAC) Matrix + Cell Types 33 Metrics Adds +12 metrics: Unlocks Cat III (Clustering: ARI, NMI, Silhouette, Davies-Bouldin) and Cat V (Biological Signal & Differential Fidelity: DE/DA score, p-value distribution score, true proportion, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC).
Single-Cell (scRNA / scATAC) Matrix + Batch Info 27 Metrics Adds +6 metrics: Unlocks Cat IV (Batch Effects: Batch Silhouette, PCR R2R^2, CMS, ISI, Seurat mixing metric, cross-batch F1).
Single-Cell (scRNA / scATAC) Full Metadata (Matrix + Cell Types + Batch) 39 Metrics Unlocks the complete unimodal suite across Categories I, II, III, IV, V, VI, and VIII.
Paired Multiomics (scRNA + scATAC - Rice Bud) RNA + ATAC Matrices alone 33 Metrics Both unimodal distributions, correlations, manifolds, trajectories PLUS Cat VI (Multiomics Integration: Batch ASW, Cell-Type ASW, Graph Connectivity, ARI, NMI, and Scalability).
Paired Multiomics (scRNA + scATAC - Rice Bud) Matrices + Cell Types 41 Metrics Unlocks Cat III clustering and Cat V biological signal fidelity across both modalities.
Paired Multiomics (scRNA + scATAC - Rice Bud) Matrices + Batch Info 39 Metrics Unlocks Cat IV batch effects and confounder integration.
Paired Multiomics (scRNA + scATAC - Rice Bud) Full Metadata (RNA + ATAC + Cell Types + Batch) All 56 Measures Complete multiomics benchmark suite across all 8 canonical categories (Categories I–VIII).
Unpaired Multiomics (Independent cells - Soybean Root) RNA + ATAC Matrices alone 27 Metrics Both unimodal distributions plus population-level integration and Scalability.
Unpaired Multiomics (Independent cells - Soybean Root) Full Metadata (RNA + ATAC + Cell Types + Batch) 41 Metrics Complete unpaired multiomics suite: Unlocks cluster concordance, donor batch integration, biological signals, and integration metrics.

3. Score Normalization and Visual Mapping Workflow

In single-cell benchmarking, metrics operate on disparate scales and directions: statistical distances are near zero (lower is better), runtime is in seconds, peak memory is in MiB, and clustering accuracy ranges in [−1,1][-1, 1] (higher is better).

scSimEval resolves this through an automated two-step score normalization pipeline:

Figure 2: Score normalization and visual mapping workflow in scSimEval. Box 1 shows the two-step normalization: direction inversion for lower-is-better metrics followed by min-max scaling to a standard [0, 1] range. Box 2 illustrates visual mapping into bubble matrices, where bubble size reflects simulation quality and top performers are highlighted with bold circular outlines.

  1. Direction Inversion: For metrics where smaller values indicate better simulations (e.g. KS distance, Wasserstein distance, RMSE, runtime, peak RAM), scores are inverted: Inverted Value=Maximum−Value\text{Inverted Value} = \text{Maximum} - \text{Value}
  2. Min-Max Scaling (0.000.00 to 1.001.00): Values are scaled so 1.001.00 universally represents best observed performance: Standardized Score=Value−MinimumMaximum−Minimum\text{Standardized Score} = \frac{\text{Value} - \text{Minimum}}{\text{Maximum} - \text{Minimum}}

In bubble matrix visualizations, bubble size directly reflects standardized quality, bold circular outlines highlight the top-performing simulator for each metric, and category colors organize the evaluation dimensions.

4. Installation and Quick Start

Install and load scSimEval from GitHub:

if (!requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("kabilanbio/scSimEval")
library(scSimEval)

scSimEval provides built-in reference datasets for instant testing: * example_scrna: Empirical reference and simulated scRNA-seq count matrices (60 genes×80 cells60\text{ genes} \times 80\text{ cells}) with cell types and batch annotations. * example_scatac: Empirical reference and simulated scATAC-seq peak matrices (60 peaks×80 cells60\text{ peaks} \times 80\text{ cells}). * example_rice_bud: Option B standardized Seurat v5 paired single-cell multiomics benchmark dataset of rice bud tissue (100 cells, 200 genes, 200 peaks, 4 cell types, 2 batches across 6 simulators). * example_soybean_root: Option B standardized Seurat v5 unpaired single-cell multiomics benchmark dataset of soybean root tissue (100 RNA cells, 100 ATAC cells, 200 genes, 200 peaks, 4 cell types, 2 batches across 3 simulators).

data(example_scrna, package = "scSimEval")
data(example_scatac, package = "scSimEval")

cat("scRNA-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scrna$ref), "\n")
#> scRNA-seq dimensions: 60 80
cat("scATAC-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scatac$ref), "\n")
#> scATAC-seq dimensions: 60 80
cat("Cell types present:", levels(example_scrna$cell_types), "\n")
#> Cell types present: TypeA TypeB

5. Evaluating Data Properties and Distributions (Categories I & II)

evaluate_simulation_accuracy() computes 1D and 2D distribution distances and zero-inflation patterns between reference and simulated matrices:

unimodal_res <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(
  ref_data = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data = example_scrna$sim,
  compute_bivariate = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Preview library size distribution metrics
lib_summary <- subset(unimodal_res$metrics_summary_table, Property == "library_size")
knitr::kable(head(lib_summary, 6), digits = 4, caption = "Library Size Statistical Distance Measures")
Library Size Statistical Distance Measures
Category Property Metric Value
Distributional Properties library_size Wasserstein 15.0625
Distributional Properties library_size KS 0.2125
Distributional Properties library_size MAD 15.0000
Distributional Properties library_size Bhattacharyya 0.0001
Distributional Properties library_size Runs_Statistic -1.7447
Distributional Properties library_size NN_Mismatch 0.1750

5.1 Comparative Distribution QC Plot (plot_distribution_qc)

plot_distribution_qc() generates a multi-panel layout comparing properties such as library size, mean expression, gene variance, zero proportions, and cell-cell correlations:

Figure 3: Comparative distribution QC layout. Compares real biological data (warm brick red) and simulated data (steel blue) across single-cell distributional properties, mean-variance trends, and zero-inflation curves. 

plot_distribution_qc(
  ref_data   = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data   = example_scrna$sim,
  title      = "Data Properties Quality Control",
  ref_name   = "Real Data",
  sim_name   = "Simulated Data",
  cell_types = example_scrna$cell_types
)

6. Evaluating Cell Clustering and Group Structure (Category III)

evaluate_clustering_metrics() assesses whether simulated data preserve unsupervised cluster separability and ground-truth cell-type boundaries:

clust_res <- evaluate_clustering_metrics(
  data = example_scrna$sim,
  cell_types = example_scrna$cell_types,
  ref_data = example_scrna$ref
)

cat("Average Silhouette Width:", round(clust_res$silhouette, 4), "\n")
#> Average Silhouette Width: 0.0034
cat("Neighborhood Purity:", round(clust_res$neighborhood_purity, 4), "\n")
#> Neighborhood Purity: 0.4775
cat("Adjusted Rand Index (ARI):", round(clust_res$ARI, 4), "\n")
#> Adjusted Rand Index (ARI): -0.0098
cat("Normalized Mutual Information (NMI):", round(clust_res$NMI, 4), "\n")
#> Normalized Mutual Information (NMI): 0.0019

7. Evaluating Batch Effects and Technical Confounders (Category IV)

evaluate_batch_metrics() checks whether simulated multi-batch data properly capture technical batch variations without obscuring biological signals:

batch_res <- evaluate_batch_metrics(
  data = example_scrna$sim,
  batch_info = example_scrna$batch_info,
  cell_types = example_scrna$cell_types,
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("Batch Silhouette:", round(batch_res$batch_silhouette, 4), "\n")
#> Batch Silhouette: -0.0027
cat("PC Regression R2 (PCR):", round(batch_res$pcr_r2, 4), "\n")
#> PC Regression R2 (PCR): 0.0095
cat("Cross-Batch Transfer F1:", round(batch_res$cross_batch_F1, 4), "\n")
#> Cross-Batch Transfer F1: 0.5126

8. Evaluating Cell Lineages and Trajectory Topology (Category VII)

scSimEval implements the standardized dynverse trajectory evaluation workflow (Saelens et al., Nature Biotechnology, 2019) specifically within Category VII (preprocess_trajectory_hvgs() + evaluate_trajectory_metrics()). Because this workflow models HVG transcriptomic expression dynamics, Category VII is evaluated on scRNA-seq only and automatically skipped for scATAC-seq:

  1. Outlier Cell & Low-Expression QC: 3-MAD outlier cell removal on library size, detected genes, and mitochondrial fraction; retains genes expressed in ≥5%\ge 5\% of cells with average expression >0.02> 0.02.
  2. HVG Selection & Zero-Convergence: Decomposes log-variance via scran::modelGeneVar (FDR < 0.05, biological variance >0.5> 0.5, with adaptive fallback on sparse test sets) and iteratively removes all-zero cells/features.
  3. Trajectory & wcor_features: Infers continuous Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) milestone graphs, evaluates him, edge_flip, geodesic_correlation, and F1_branches, and trains ranger Random Forests (num_trees = 10000, mtry = 1% of HVGs, importance = "impurity") predicting cell-to-milestone geodesic distances to compute reference-weighted wcor_features.
traj_res <- evaluate_trajectory_metrics(
  ref_data = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data = example_scrna$sim,
  cell_types_ref = example_scrna$cell_types,
  cell_types_sim = example_scrna$cell_types,
  num_trees = 500L
)

cat("HIM Topology Similarity:", round(traj_res$him, 4), "\n")
#> HIM Topology Similarity: 1
cat("Edge Flip Similarity:", round(traj_res$edge_flip, 4), "\n")
#> Edge Flip Similarity: 1
cat("Geodesic Distance Correlation:", round(traj_res$geodesic_correlation, 4), "\n")
#> Geodesic Distance Correlation: 0.4849
cat("Branch Assignment F1:", round(traj_res$F1_branches, 4), "\n")
#> Branch Assignment F1: 1
cat("Dynamic Feature Importance wCor:", round(traj_res$wcor_features, 4), "\n")
#> Dynamic Feature Importance wCor: 0.194

9. Evaluating Biological Signal and Differential Fidelity (Category V)

evaluate_deg_fidelity() evaluates whether simulated counts preserve true differential expression signals (SimBench DE, DP, DV, DD, BD), cell-type classification accuracy, and top-DEG Jaccard overlap:

deg_res <- evaluate_deg_fidelity(
  ref_data      = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data      = example_scrna$sim,
  ref_celltypes = example_scrna$cell_types,
  sim_celltypes = example_scrna$cell_types,
  top_n_de      = 50
)
knitr::kable(head(deg_res$deg_summary_table, 6), digits = 4)

10. Evaluating Computational Scalability & Efficiency (Category VIII)

plot_scalability_benchmark() generates a comprehensive dashboard comparing core-normalized CPU execution time (Core-Seconds, Elapsed Time×Ncores\text{Elapsed Time} \times N_{\text{cores}}), per-core memory demand (Peak RAM per Allocated Core, Peak RAM/Ncores\text{Peak RAM} / N_{\text{cores}} in MiB/core or GiB/core), Bivariate Core-Seconds vs. Memory per Core tradeoff frontiers, and normalized resource cost:

Figure 4: Computational scalability benchmark suite. Multi-panel dashboard comparing cumulative CPU work (Core-Seconds), per-core peak RAM footprint (MiB/core), resource tradeoff frontiers, and normalized resource cost across simulation methods. 

data(example_rice_bud, package = "scSimEval")
plot_scalability_benchmark(example_rice_bud$scalability_benchmarks)

11. Master Multiomics Pipeline: evaluate_multiomics_accuracy

The flagship pipeline function evaluate_multiomics_accuracy() executes the complete benchmark across all 8 canonical categories in a single call:

data(example_rice_bud, package = "scSimEval")

# Option B Seurat v5 objects embed counts, cell_type, batch, and integrated reductions
master_eval <- evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(
  ref_multi    = example_rice_bud$reference$combined,
  sim_multi    = example_rice_bud$simulated$scMultiSim$combined,
  pairing      = "paired",
  elapsed_time = 12.4,
  memory_mb    = 248,
  verbose      = FALSE
)

# Tidy summary table containing the evaluated benchmark metrics
head(master_eval$metrics_summary_table)

HPC Multi-Core Parallelization: Specifying threads = 4 or threads = 8 parallelizes 2D distribution tests and cross-modal peak-to-gene correlations via BiocParallel.

12. Visualization Suite

scSimEval provides built-in visualization functions generating publication-ready figures (supporting 600 DPI export).

12.1 Multi-Dimensional Benchmarking Bubble Matrix (plot_benchmark_bubble_matrix)

The flagship visualization plot_benchmark_bubble_matrix() summarizes multi-simulator performance across the 8 evaluation categories. Bubble sizes represent standardized simulation quality (0.000.00 to 1.001.00; larger is better), and top performers for each metric are highlighted with bold circular outlines:

Figure 5: Flagship multi-dimensional benchmarking bubble matrix. Ranks simulation methods top-to-bottom across the 8 evaluation categories based on the 56 curated evaluation metric analysis. Bubble sizes indicate standardized fidelity scores (0.000.00 to 1.001.00), and top performers for each metric are highlighted with bold circular outlines. 

# Render benchmark bubble matrix
plot_benchmark_bubble_matrix(
  data = demo_benchmark_results,
  bubble_size_range = c(2, 7.5),
  title = "Benchmarking Single-Cell Simulation Methods (56 Curated Evaluation Suite)",
  subtitle = "Comparative performance across 8 evaluation categories"
)

12.2 Evaluation Summary Horizontal Bar Matrix (plot_evaluation_summary)

plot_evaluation_summary() ranks candidate simulators from best to worst and displays average scores across all evaluation categories:

Figure 6: Executive evaluation summary horizontal bar matrix. Ranks simulators across the 8 categories and displays overall composite performance with exact score annotations. 

# Extract method leaderboard
leaderboard <- compute_method_leaderboard(demo_benchmark_results)
knitr::kable(leaderboard, digits = 4, caption = "Simulator Performance Leaderboard")

12.3 Metric Score Distributions Across Categories (plot_metric_boxplots)

plot_metric_boxplots() displays score distributions and individual metric data points across the 8 categories:

Figure 7: Metric score distributions across the 8 categories. Displays standardized scores ([0,1][0, 1], higher is better) with individual data points and boxplots across candidate simulators.

12.4 Complete Benchmark Heatmap (plot_metric_heatmap)

plot_metric_heatmap() displays exact numeric values for every metric inside each cell:

Figure 8: Complete benchmark metric heatmap. Displays exact unnormalized raw scores in bold text inside every cell, grouped across the 8 evaluation categories.

12.5 Dimension Reduction and Ordination Plots (PCA & MDS)

plot_metric_pca() and plot_metric_mds() project simulation methods into 2D metric ordination space:

Figure 9: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) ordination of simulation methods. Projects simulators based on their metric profiles, showing algorithmic affinities and key discriminating metric vectors.

12.6 Cell Embeddings (t-SNE, UMAP, & PCA) and Low-Dimensional Quality Metrics

scSimEval enables visual and quantitative inspection of whether simulated cells faithfully recover biological manifolds:

# Compute low-dimensional embeddings
emb_data <- compute_dataset_embeddings(
  reference   = example_scrna$ref,
  simulated   = list("Splatter" = example_scrna$sim),
  reduction   = "pca",
  n_pcs       = 10,
  cell_types  = example_scrna$cell_types,
  batch       = example_scrna$batch_info
)

# Quantitative low-dimensional quality metrics
quality_table <- compute_embedding_quality_metrics(emb_data)
knitr::kable(quality_table, digits = 4, caption = "Quantitative Low-Dimensional Quality Metrics")
Quantitative Low-Dimensional Quality Metrics
Dataset Role Cells (N) Mean Silhouette ARI (Cluster Fidelity) Mean Library Size Mean Detected Features Library Size Diff (%)
Reference Reference 80 -0.0101 -0.0067 256.3 49.2 0.00
Splatter Simulated 80 0.0037 -0.0071 242.3 48.3 5.46

13. Multi-Dataset and Multi-Method Benchmarking

For studies evaluating simulators across multiple biological cohorts or tissues, scSimEval provides automated multi-dataset tools:

# Combine independent benchmark sessions into a unified multi-dataset object
multi_bench <- combine_benchmark_results(
  benchmark_rice,
  benchmark_soybean,
  dataset_names = c("Rice Bud (Paired)", "Soybean Root (Unpaired)")
)

# Compute cross-dataset average fidelity leaderboard
compute_method_leaderboard(multi_bench)

# Step-by-step interactive figure zoom (+30% magnification)
p_zoomed <- zoom_plot(p_bubble, zoom = 1.3)

14. Interactive Web Application (Shiny Studio)

For researchers who prefer a graphical interface, launch_scSimEval_app() opens the interactive Benchmarking Studio:

# Launch interactive Shiny studio in default browser
launch_scSimEval_app()

The studio is organized into 8 modular tabs: 1. Home: Overview of the 56 curated evaluation measures and interactive tour. 2. Data Hub: 4 ingestion modes (Demo benchmark data, Single-cell evaluation, Multi-omics co-assays, and Upload saved results) with QC inspection and automated SLURM script generation. 3. Comparative Bubble Matrix & Leaderboard: 56-metric matrix with multi-dataset selectors, step-by-step zoom, podium rankings, and standalone R script download. 4. Visualizations: Diagnostic panels for Evaluation Summary, Distribution QC, Scalability, Metric Boxplots, Heatmaps, PCA/MDS, and Cell Embeddings. 5. Results & Export: Dual-value table reporting (Score_Raw and normalized Score) with Excel, CSV, RDS, and ZIP export handlers. 6. Help & Manual: Formula glossary, hardware recommendations, and input templates. 7. Logs & Diagnostics: Real-time event streaming and diagnostic tracebacks. 8. About & Authors: Complete author team profiles, institutional details, and academic citation links.

15. Supported Multiomics Data Types and Metric Compatibility

15.1 Two Experimental Designs

scSimEval strictly evaluates single-cell multiomics simulations according to experimental design:

Data Type Definition Example Technologies
Paired RNA and ATAC measured from exactly the same cells 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq
Unpaired RNA and ATAC measured from separate cells of the same tissue Independent 10x scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq experiments

15.2 Metric Compatibility by Data Type

Evaluation Dimension & Metric Group Paired Multiomics Unpaired Multiomics Unimodal (scRNA / scATAC)
(I) Distributional Properties (10 univariate + 4 bivariate across 7 cell, 7 feature, and 4 bivariate pairs) ✅ (All 14) ✅ (All 14) ✅ (All 14)
(II) Sparsity & Zero-Inflation Dynamics (Logistic dropout midpoint/slope/R2R^2, accessibility-sparsity RMSE/R2R^2, excess zero weights) ✅ (All 5) ✅ (All 5) ✅ (3 scRNA / 3 scATAC)
(III) Cellular Manifold & Clustering Concordance (MMD, Generative Precision/Recall, Silhouette ASW, CDI, Neighborhood Purity, ARI, NMI) ✅ (All 8) ✅ (All 8) ✅ (All 8)
(IV) Technical Variation & Batch Mixing Dynamics (Batch Silhouette, PCR R2R^2, CMS, ISI, Cross-batch F1) ✅ (All 5) ✅ (All 5) ✅ (All 5)
(V) Biological Signal & Differential Fidelity (Parallel scRNA-seq DE [6] and scATAC-seq DA [6] pseudobulk edgeR-QLF suites) ✅ (All 12) ✅ (All 12) ✅ (6 per modality)
(VI) Multiomics Integration & Alignment (batch_asw, cell_type_asw, graph_connectivity, ari, nmi) ✅ (All 5) ✅ (All 5) ❌ (Multiomics only)
(VII) Trajectory & Lineage Topology (him, edge_flip, geodesic_correlation, F1_branches, wcor_features) ✅ (All 5, scRNA-seq) ✅ (All 5, scRNA-seq) ✅ (5 scRNA / ❌ scATAC)
(VIII) Computational Scalability & Efficiency (core_seconds, memory_per_core_mib) ✅ (Both 2) ✅ (Both 2) ✅ (Both 2)
Total Evaluation Capacity All 56 Measures All 56 Measures 40 (scRNA) / 35 (scATAC)
Direct Pipeline Support evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(..., pairing="paired") evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(..., pairing="unpaired") evaluate_simulation_accuracy()

15.3 Recommended Workflows by Data Type

Paired data — run the master multiomics pipeline directly:

evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(
  ref_multi = list(rna = ref_rna, atac = ref_atac),
  sim_multi = list(rna = sim_rna, atac = sim_atac),
  cell_types = cell_types,
  batch_info = batch_info,
  pairing = "paired"
)

Unpaired data — run the master multiomics pipeline with pairing = "unpaired":

evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(
  ref_multi = list(rna = ref_rna, atac = ref_atac),
  sim_multi = list(rna = sim_rna, atac = sim_atac),
  cell_types = list(rna = rna_cell_types, atac = atac_cell_types),
  batch_info = list(rna = rna_batches, atac = atac_batches),
  pairing = "unpaired"
)

16. Large-Scale Multi-Dataset Benchmarking on HPC Clusters

When evaluating simulation tools across multiple biological cohorts (e.g. 6 simulators across 16 datasets), benchmark_simulation_suite() optimizes memory management and cluster multithreading:

# Run high-performance multi-dataset benchmark
mset_bench <- benchmark_simulation_suite(
  datasets    = refs,
  simulators  = sims,
  threads     = 8,
  auto_sparse = TRUE,
  run_gc      = TRUE,
  save_path   = "my_multidataset_benchmark.rds"
)

# Plot consolidated bubble matrix
plot_benchmark_bubble_matrix(mset_bench)

17. Summary

scSimEval provides a unified, objective, and reference-based evaluation framework for benchmarking single-cell and multiomics simulation methods. With 56 curated evaluation measures across 8 foundational categories, automated score normalization, and publication-quality visualizations, it enables researchers to rigorously validate simulation tools with confidence.
